GET /api/orders/[id] fetches the order with prisma.order.findUnique({where:{id}}) using the attacker-supplied path id and no userId predicate; any authenticated user can read any order's customer email and delivery address. The check at line 60 (order.userId !== user.id) only appends a flag instead of blocking access, so no predicate binds the selected order to the authenticated user.

Accept decision after `prisma.supportAccessToken` lookup never checks the record's expiry field, though a sibling mutation on the same model sets it.

POST /api/user/support-access lets the caller supply an arbitrary targetEmail (defaulting to their own), resolves that attacker-selected user at prisma.user.findUnique({where:{email:targetEmail}}), and creates a SupportAccessToken bound to targetUser.id (line 73-80), returning the token and /support-login URL. No check binds the target user to the authenticated caller, so an attacker can mint a support token for any user (e.g. an admin) and log in as them via /api/auth/support-login.
Protected data is written to durable storage without encryption or hashing: 'token' is a freshly generated reusable credential written to durable storage in plaintext instead of as a one-way hash.

The attempted check at line 72 (wishlist.userId !== user.id) merely discloses a flag and does not abort the read.
